title: DecisionModelBench: Empirical Benchmark of Non-Autoregressive Decision Models vs Foundation LLMs in Cyber-Physical Systems, Algorithmic Trading, and Civic Emergency Triage
description:
DecisionModelBench is an empirical benchmark platform and scientific research repository evaluating Non-Autoregressive Decision Models (System 1) against Foundation Generative Large Language Models (System 2) across dual NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU distributed topologies.

This deposition contains the complete reproducible experimental codebase, multi-GPU sharding pipelines, simulation engines, dataset results, and two foundational scientific research papers authored by Richie O. Sumual (PANITA GORONTALO):

  1. Paper 1: The Autoregression Fallacy in Time-Critical Cyber-Physical Systems and Algorithmic Trading: An Empirical Benchmark of Non-Autoregressive Decision Models versus Foundation Large Language Models (English & Indonesian editions, PDF & LaTeX).
  2. Paper 2: Deterministic Intent Gating, Sovereign Emergency Calling, and Two-Tier Civic Triage: An Empirical Evaluation of Non-Autoregressive Decision Models versus Foundation Large Language Models in Municipal 911/112 Operations and High-Throughput Public Administration (English & Indonesian editions, PDF & LaTeX).

Key Empirical Findings

  • Sub-100 ms Reflex Triage: Compact non-autoregressive models (Laya 421M ModernBERT at 35–55 ms, OpenJev 0.5B at 180–240 ms, TypeSafe JEV at 160 ms) achieve sub-second determinism with 0 output tokens.
  • Autoregression Fallacy Demarcation: Standalone autoregressive LLMs (Sahabat-AI 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 2 9B) incur multi-second memory bandwidth bottlenecks (2,200 ms to 12,680 ms), inducing catastrophic state-decision drift in air defense, -$19.41 P&L slippage in trading, and Erlang-C queue explosions in emergency hotlines.
  • Decoupled Two-Tier Architecture: Demonstrates that decoupling sub-100ms deterministic triage (System 1) from asynchronous conversational deliberation (System 2) resolves statutory SLA violations (<3s in 911/112 dispatch) and saves 80%–100% of GPU compute costs.

Portal & Interactive Simulations: https://tuwiliyt.github.io/decisionmodelbench/
